messages.content: I need all pending and active mandates of users parath and bhanu

function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.reasoning:
We need to call user_mandates twice? Actually we need all pending and active mandates of users parath and bhanu. So we need to fetch mandates for each user with status pending or active. We can call user_mandates twice: once for parath, once for bhanu. But we might also combine? The function only accepts one status at a time. So we need two calls per user? Wait the function signature: name, status optional. It returns mandates for that user with given status. So if we want both pending and active, we could call twice per user: once with status=active, once with status=pending. Or we could call with no status to get all? But we want only pending and active. If we call with no status, it defaults to active. So we need to call with status=active and status=pending separately.

Thus total four calls: user_mandates(parath, active), user_mandates(parath, pending), user_mandates(bhanu, active), user_mandates(bhanu, pending). Then we need to aggregate results. We'll do that.
